title: Cloudflare Pay-Per-Crawl: Income or Spare Change?
quote: more proof-of-concept than payroll [...] When an AI bot knocks on your site, Cloudflare checks the rule you set: let it in, block it, or make it pay. [...] Bot traffic typically represents only 1-2% of page views; on one million monthly views ~10,000-20,000 bot hits; at $0.001 per page ~$20 monthly, at $0.01 ~$200; a single subscriber is worth $50-$100 annually.

title: Introducing pay per crawl: Enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers for access
quote: crawler-price: signals that payment is required for the requested resource [...] a crawler can preemptively include a crawler-max-price header in its initial request [...] Publishers will then have three distinct options for a crawler: Allow, Charge, Require payment at the configured, domain-wide price. [...] Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record for pay per crawl [...] Pay per crawl, in private beta [...] an agentic world where intelligent agents can programmatically negotiate access to digital resources.

title: Content Independence Day: no AI crawl without compensation
quote: changing the default to block AI crawlers unless they pay creators for their content [...] OpenAI: 750 times more difficult to get traffic than it was with the Google of old; Anthropic: 30,000 times more difficult [...] content is the fuel that powers AI engines, and so it is only fair that content creators are compensated directly for it

title: The crawl-to-click gap: Cloudflare data on AI bots, training, and referrals
quote: Anthropic remains the most crawl-heavy platform. Even after an 87% decline this year, it still crawled 38,000 pages for every referred page visit in July 2025. OpenAI 1,091:1; Perplexity 194:1; Microsoft 40.7:1; Google 5.4:1. [...] Training now drives nearly 80% of AI bot activity, up from 72% a year ago. [...] GPTBot 11.9% -> 28.1%, ClaudeBot 15% -> 23.3% of AI crawler traffic.

title: Cloudflare, Coinbase and the x402 Foundation
quote: Cloudflare is partnering with Coinbase to create the x402 Foundation. [...] crawlers participating in our private beta of pay per crawl are able to crawl a vast number of pages easily, generate audit logs, and then be charged a single fee via a connected credit card or bank account at the end of each day. [...] We will be bringing this new deferred payment scheme to pay per crawl as we expand and evolve the private beta.

title: Cloudflare new policy pushes AI companies to pay for publishers content
quote: Cloudflare will block mixed-use crawlers from ad-hosted pages by default [from September 15], affecting new customers, new sites, and all free-tier users. [...] expanding beyond Pay Per Crawl into Pay Per Use [...] Over 50% of AI crawler traffic involves re-fetching unchanged pages. [...] Ceramic.ai and You.com are the first partners in the Pay Per Use model. Prince: Now that the majority of traffic on the Internet is non-human, we must go further and act faster so that a sustainable ecosystem can emerge.

title: Cloudflare stops charging AI per crawl and starts paying per answer
quote: crawling was a poor proxy for value, because a single page might be crawled once and then cited in thousands of AI-generated answers, or crawled repeatedly and never cited at all. [...] 57.4% of web traffic to HTML content was bot-generated across the Cloudflare network by early June 2026; 50.6% of that traffic came from training-related crawlers; 10.7% from search-related bots. [...] Cloudflare describes the entire effort as an experiment

title: Cloudflare Allows the Agentic Internet to Flourish with a Simple Philosophy: Your Content, Your Rules
quote: Pay Per Use: evolution of Pay Per Crawl so publishers are paid when their content creates value. [...] mixed crawlers will be blocked on pages with ads [September 15, 2026]. [...] Over 50 major content licensing agreements signed in the past year. [...] 50% of crawl traffic from AI crawlers spent re-fetching unchanged pages. Partners: Ceramic.ai, You.com, beehiiv, Conde Nast, Patreon.

title: Why Stack Overflow and Cloudflare launched a pay-per-crawl model
quote: protect our data against commercial usage for model training, but also still allowing access to our community [...] they are eating up ad impressions [...] when we turned on Pay Per Crawl... they stopped sending traffic our way. So it is almost like they got the message. [...] more and more these 402s will help drive conversion, and the humans behind these bots will provide payment information

title: What is Pay Per Crawl? — Cloudflare AI Crawl Control docs
quote: Pay per crawl is currently in closed beta. [...] setting a price per zone [...] crawlers either present payment intent via request headers for successful HTTP 200 access, or receive an HTTP 402 Payment Required response with pricing. [...] Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record

title: The next step for content creators in working with AI bots: Introducing AI Crawl Control
quote: Today, we are rebranding our AI Audit tool as AI Crawl Control and moving it from beta to general availability. [...] select individual bots to block with a configurable message parameter and send 402 payment required responses [...] To access this content, email partnerships@yoursite.com or call 1-800-LICENSE. [...] pay per crawl continues advancing through beta

title: AI bot traffic closing in on human web visits, study finds (TollBit State of the Bots Q3/Q4 2025)
quote: one AI bot visit for every 31 human visits (Q4 2025), up from one bot visit for every 200 human visits (Q1 2025). [...] human visitors to websites declined by five percent [Q3 to Q4 2025]. Training scrapes dropped by 15 percent between Q2 and Q4; RAG bot traffic increased by 33 percent. [...] Clickthrough rates fell from 0.8 percent in Q2 2025 to just 0.27 percent in Q4

title: New RSL Web Standard and Collective Rights Organization Automate Content Licensing for the AI-First Internet
quote: [September 10, 2025] Reddit, People Inc., Yahoo, Internet Brands, Ziff Davis, Fastly, Quora, O Reilly Media, Medium [...] licensing options: free, attribution, subscription, pay-per-crawl, pay-per-inference (publishers compensated when AI applications use their content to generate responses). [...] RSL goes beyond robots.txt by enabling machine-readable licensing and royalty terms

title: Reddit, Yahoo, Medium and more are adopting a new licensing standard to get compensated for AI scraping
quote: RSL adds licensing terms to the robots.txt protocol [...] Cloudflare, which recently launched a pay-per-crawl system, could eventually play a part, too. [...] the RSL Collective is partnering with Fastly for technical enforcement, with Leeds describing it as the bouncer at the door to the club.

title: AI Preferences (aipref) Working Group charter
quote: A standard track document covering vocabulary for expressing AI-related preferences, independent of how those preferences are associated with content. [...] Out of scope: Technical enforcement of preferences; Application layer protocols for authenticating or authorizing clients and/or crawlers; Auditing and other transparency measures for AI training

title: Google strikes $60 million deal with Reddit, allowing search giant to train AI models on human posts
quote: [February 23, 2024] valued at roughly $60 million [...] use posts from the online discussion site for training its artificial intelligence models and to improve services such as Google Search

title: Cloudflare new plan could change how AI pays publishers
quote: once captured by an AI crawler, a piece of content could be used multiple times, in hundreds or even thousands of answers. On the other hand, something could be crawled and never used at all. [...] companies will always choose to get the best/most data for the least cost [...] whether it is less costly to get the data they want via Cloudflare system. If it is not, it will remain merely an experiment. [...] micropayments historically failed because the revenue from a small payment by a single customer was never worth the processing hassle

title: Cloudflare gives AI crawlers a September deadline: pay publishers or get blocked
quote: From 15 September, new Cloudflare sites will keep letting search engines index their pages. They will block AI training and AI agents from any page with advertising by default. [...] If a crawler will not let a site owner separate those uses, it gets blocked on ad-supported pages. [...] compensating publishers when their content shapes an AI answer, not just when it is fetched.

title: Web Bot Auth — Cloudflare Bots docs
quote: Web Bot Auth is an authentication method that leverages cryptographic signatures in HTTP messages to verify that a request comes from an automated bot. [...] Cloudflare supports Ed25519 key algorithm [...] key directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory [...] relies on two IETF drafts: a directory draft for the crawler to share their public keys, and a protocol draft defining how these keys should be used

title: HTTP Message Signatures for automated traffic: Architecture (draft-meunier-web-bot-auth-architecture-05)
quote: This document describes an architecture for identifying automated traffic using HTTP Message Signatures. [...] User-Agent, when used alone, can be spoofed meaning anyone may attempt to act as that agent [...] Individual Internet-Draft, version 05, published March 2, 2026, expired September 3, 2026; replaced by draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol.

title: Discover payable content — Pay Per Crawl Discovery API
quote: The API returns a list of zones (domains) that have Pay Per Crawl enabled [...] All requests to the Discovery API must be authenticated using HTTP message signatures with Web Bot Auth headers

title: Beyond block or allow: How pay-per-crawl is reshaping public data monetization
quote: You are welcome to come get this if there is some sort of payment that happens in here. [Will Allen, Cloudflare] [...] complements, not replaces, traditional data licensing. [...] We are basically just playing whack-a-mole. [Josh Zhang]

title: Announcing the Monetization Gateway: charge for any resource behind Cloudflare via x402
quote: [July 1, 2026] an engine that will give Cloudflare customers the ability to charge for any asset protected by Cloudflare: web pages, datasets, APIs, or MCP tools. [...] payments will settle in stablecoins over x402 [...] $0.01 for every GET or POST request [...] $0.001 base fee plus $0.01 per MB charge [...] The Monetization Gateway waitlist is open now

title: zeen101/leaky-paywall: The #1 metered paywall for WordPress
quote: The #1 metered paywall for WordPress. Sell subscriptions without sacrificing search and social visibility. [...] launch a metered paywall, grow your email list with a registration wall

title: Set a pay per crawl price — Cloudflare docs
quote: The minimum price is $0.001 USD per crawl. This is the amount charged for each successful content retrieval (HTTP 200 response) by an AI crawler.

title: Pay Per Crawl enhancements (changelog, 2025-12-10)
quote: A new authenticated API endpoint allows verified crawlers to programmatically discover domains participating in Pay Per Crawl [...] Payment headers must now be included in the Web Bot Auth signature-input header components [...] crawler-error header with 11 specific error codes [...] Site owners can now offer free access to specific pages

title: Making AI search smarter (Content Independence Day 2026)
quote: [2026-07-01] more than 50% of crawl traffic from good bots goes to re-fetching pages that have not changed [...] a real start, but crawling is a crude measure of value [...] publishers who opt in can be paid when their content appears in Ceramic search results [...] agents can pay on demand for a specific piece of premium content they need, without any upfront commitment [You.com] [...] payment is designed to follow the value the work delivers rather than the number of times a crawler happens to fetch it

title: The crawl before the fall of referrals: understanding AI impact on content providers
quote: [June 19-26, 2025] Anthropic (Claude): 70,900:1; Mistral: 0.1:1. [...] The ratio divides total number of requests from relevant user agents [...] by total number of requests for HTML content where the Referer header contained a hostname associated with a given search or AI platform. [...] these figures may overstate actual ratios because native app traffic lacks Referer headers

title: Cloudflare says bot blocking is fuelling publisher AI deals
quote: We have seen lots of our customers use our tools so that they can create reliable scarcity for their content, and then negotiate better deals. [Stephanie Cohen] [...] Financial Times, The Atlantic, Ziff Davis, Conde Nast and Associated Press. [...] People are understanding the value of our content because we are able to restrict almost everybody from using our content using our Cloudflare blocking. And they have to pay for it. [Neil Vogel, People Inc]

title: News Corp eyes multi-LLM licensing strategy after $250 million OpenAI deal
quote: inked its first major AI content licensing deal with OpenAI in May 2024 — estimated to be worth around $250 million over five years [...] woo and sue

title: 402 Payment Required — HTTP reference (MDN)
quote: This status code was created to enable digital cash or (micro) payment systems and would indicate that requested content is not available until the client makes a payment. No standard use convention exists [...] This status code is reserved but not defined. [...] No browser supports a 402
